budget_policy: contract default is 12 per family; this direction was scoped by its task to trial_count <= 4; every bounded audit attempt is recorded below including the failed one
selection_decision: No return candidate was ever produced, so there is nothing to select. Verdict across all 4 trials: the direction is 'blocked' at the data gate (development-window GDELT coverage and a lawful point-in-time price panel do not exist locally); the 2-slice replay-audit rules are frozen and structurally validated for any future rerun.

trials.name: structural_parse_unregistered_2022_slice
trials.method: In-memory unzip + tab-join parse; assert single member, tab-delimited, 61 columns; map GDELT Export v2 columns (GLOBALEVENTID, SQLDATE, Actor1/2Code, EventCode, GoldsteinScale, NumMentions/Sources/Articles, AvgTone, DATEADDED, SOURCEURL); count distinct DATEADDED/SQLDATE/URL/host/actor values; dedup-key collision counts under (DATEADDED, url); GLOBALEVENTID uniqueness.
trials.result: PASS structurally: 1184 rows x 61 cols (all rows), one member, DATEADDED singleton 20220809030000 == filename bucket; GLOBALEVENTID unique 1184/1184; (DATEADDED,url) keys 244 distinct vs 1184 rows (182 collided keys; 79.4% row redundancy); distinct hosts 119/244 URLs; Actor1Code present 1038 (87.7%), Actor2Code 855 (72.2%), both 709 (59.9%); mention/tone fields present in 100% of rows; SQLDATE never forward of DATEADDED, backward lags reach 366 days (14 rows dated 20210809).
trials.provenance_caveat: No upstream md5 available offline for this unregistered file (would have required a network request, which this task forbids and none was made). All coverage numbers derived from it are therefore fixture-grade, not evidence-grade, until re-derived from manifested slices.
trials.influence_on_packages: Motivated frozen rules: within-slice dedup identity, Actor1Code->host fallback entity rule, and the explicit SQLDATE max-lag requirement (naive same-day SQLDATE join falsified as a design choice).

trials.name: structural_parse_canonical_2026_slice
trials.method: Same bounded parse as T01 on a slice whose provenance IS recorded (data/manifest.json, sha256-verified against manifest before parsing); cross-check lastupdate.txt content against the on-slice bucket.
trials.result: PASS structurally and on provenance: zip sha256 003f2e6ea6316482c1595c5235657ddd731361bfdf60c9948553a947f5d03b2e matches manifest; lastupdate.txt sha256 d9160dc7180a05da2bc9df5c6a7b947682b9328fe2c2b2dee9cbfa1fb1ff9f6e matches manifest and lists export/mentions/gkg all for bucket 20260829231500 with the next export bucket 20260829231500->23231500 pattern identical to the csv filename convention; slice parses as 464 rows x 61 cols, DATEADDED singleton == filename bucket, GLOBALEVENTID 464/464 unique, (DATEADDED,url) 109 distinct keys (76.5% redundancy), hosts 60/109, Actor1Code 424 (91.4%), mention fields 100% present; SQLDATE never forward of DATEADDED (2 earlier-day rows).
trials.influence_on_packages: Confirmed the slice clock rule (DATEADDED == bucket) on a provenanced file and fixed the upstream-material fingerprint convention used in strategy.json.data_used.

trials.name: upstream_md5_semantics_probe
trials.method: Hypothesis H1: upstream_md5 is md5 of the extracted CSV (GDELT docs describe per-file md5 for export tables). Compute md5(export.CSV) via unzip pipe and via Python zipfile; compare to 56a02e3b....
trials.result: H1 FAILED and was superseded by H2: md5(CSV) = 902c2e927eced2173d0e2eef09d8773f != 56a02e3b605f81fbf2e440b2cc676496 (both shell and Python agree, so the discrepancy is semantic, not computational). H2: md5(zip file) = 56a02e3b605f81fbf2e440b2cc676496 exactly matches manifest upstream_md5, the manifest etag, and lastupdate.txt's number. GDELT 2.0 publishes md5-of-zip; the manifest already encoded this correctly via its etag and verified_upstream_md5 flags.
trials.failed_aspect: Initial interpretation (md5-of-inner-CSV) was wrong; corrected within the same bounded session, no further data touched.
trials.influence_on_packages: Freezes the fingerprint rule for the strategy.json falsification gate: future backfill must verify md5-of-zip against GDELT/LASTUPDATE numbers, and the inner-CSV md5 must never be compared to upstream_md5.

trials.name: coverage_gate_feasibility_check
trials.input: Full local inventory: data/manifest.json files[] (gdelt subset = 2 files, 29868 bytes), explorations/event-semantics tree (1 zip + empty output/ and data/gdelt_bulk/), workspace.json rank-5 entry, protocol-amendment exclusion list
trials.method: Enumerate every already-present artifact; hash and cross-check each against the manifest; determine whether ANY bounded local combination supports development-window (2020-08-01..2023-12-31) or validation-window (2024) event-coverage measurement or a returns series; explicitly check the three acceptance alternatives (normalize existing empirical returns / remove files / mark blocked).
trials.result: BLOCKED, honestly: local GDELT content = 2 single-minute slices (2022-08-09 03:00, 2026-08-29 23:15), i.e. zero coverage over the development AND validation windows and ~8 orders of magnitude short of the ~117k slices a development backfill needs; no SEC artifact exists ('SEC bulk' is a manifest intentional_omissions entry), no point-in-time price panel is referenced by any file here, no run.py/returns.csv was ever produced by the cancelled collector (output/ is empty), and fabricating either is contract-forbidden. Therefore: no empirical return series exists to normalize (option 3 of the acceptance does not apply), no file was removed, and the direction is marked 'blocked' with a concrete falsification/data gate in strategy.json.first_falsification_gate.
trials.influence_on_packages: Directly produced strategy.json.status='blocked', the data_precondition wording of the gate, and the next_experiment backfill specification.

variants_considered_but_not_run: Normalizing a fabricated or reconstructed returns series to the contract -- rejected: violates the task's no-fabrication constraint and the contract's no-synthetic-substitution rule.
Deleting the unregistered 2022 fixture to 'clean' the directory -- rejected: acceptance criterion requires removing no files; it is preserved in place, untrusted-but-parsable, and re-derivable.
Building an LLM signal or resuming collection -- out of scope by task definition and by the protocol amendment's basis for excluding this direction.
